failures.resolution: The sentence stated the avoid intent, so Gemini acting (add_to_avoid) alongside the food_search block was acceptable model behaviour; the case now asks for a lookup before deciding: 'show me watermelon in the catalog so I can decide whether to avoid it'.
The sentence explicitly asks to put greek yogurt on Eats; Gemini did so (add_to_eats) with the food_search block and named the dairy off-plan mark. The case now expects add_to_eats plus the block.

Gemini answered 'should I eat more protein or more fibre?' directly and correctly (protein first, 102 g remaining) instead of offering quick replies — acceptable. Mitigation: the case now asks explicitly for two or three quick options to pick from, which is what the quick_replies block is for; the prompt is unchanged.

The reworded sentence asked for 'two or three quick options', which in a food coach means meal options; Gemini answered correctly with three composed meals and a food_ideas block. quick_replies is for a clarifying question with choices, so the case now asks 'can you change my breakfast?' (move it, swap the foods, or skip it) and keeps the quick_replies expectation; id kept for history.

Third failure of the quick_replies kind with the block's own trigger present (the coach asked a clarifying question with no choices). Prompt guidance now binds quick_replies to the coach's own question in the same step with 2–4 choices; regression test pins the wording; wire.ts untouched.

First failure of this kind: for 'how did this week go?' Gemini called get_week_totals but not show_chart (the two earlier passes called both) and its reply still said 'Here is your calorie breakdown for the week'. Prompt unchanged on one occurrence. Mitigation noted for follow-up: extend the no-unsupported-claim verifier to block claims (a reply that says 'here is your chart/breakdown' must carry a block).
